description.short_caption: Skin biopsy showing inflammatory infiltrate (H and E stain).
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of skin stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H and E). The dermis contains a dense inflammatory infiltrate composed predominantly of lymphocytes, with some plasma cells and histiocytes. The surrounding dermal collagen appears pink and eosinophilic, with no significant necrosis or granuloma formation visible. The epidermis is not included in this section.

description.short_caption: Erythematous skin lesions with central necrosis on the upper arm.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the upper arm with multiple erythematous lesions of varying sizes. One lesion has a central area of necrosis or ulceration, while others appear as smaller red macules or papules. The surrounding skin is unremarkable, with no visible swelling or significant discoloration beyond the lesions.
visible_findings: central necrosis or ulceration in one lesion
no surrounding swelling or significant discoloration

description.short_caption: Skin biopsy with H&E stain showing epidermal and dermal inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a skin biopsy stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The epidermis appears disrupted, with evidence of inflammatory infiltrates extending into the dermis. The dermis shows dense inflammatory cell clusters, likely composed of lymphocytes and other immune cells. There is also evidence of edema and possible vascular involvement. The staining highlights cellular and structural details, aiding in the identification of pathological changes.

description.short_caption: Skin biopsy showing epidermal and dermal changes (H and E stain).
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of skin stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H and E). The epidermis appears hyperplastic with acanthosis, and there is a dense inflammatory infiltrate in the dermis. The infiltrate is composed of mixed inflammatory cells, including lymphocytes and possibly neutrophils. The overlying stratum corneum appears intact, and there is no evidence of ulceration. The image highlights both epidermal and dermal involvement, consistent with an inflammatory or infectious process.
visible_findings: mixed inflammatory cells in the dermis

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing normal lung fields and mediastinal structures.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing clear lung fields with no visible consolidations, masses, or effusions. The heart size appears within normal limits, and the mediastinal contours are unremarkable. The bony structures, including the ribs and clavicles, appear intact. There is no evidence of pneumothorax or other acute abnormalities.

description.short_caption: Skin biopsy with H&E stain at low power.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a low-power view of a skin biopsy stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The epidermis and dermis are visible, with areas of inflammation and architectural disruption. The pink eosinophilic staining highlights connective tissue, while the purple hematoxylin staining emphasizes nuclei. The overall pattern suggests a pathological process, possibly infectious or inflammatory in nature.

description.short_caption: Skin lesion with central eschar and surrounding erythema on the upper arm.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a close-up of the skin on the upper arm. A central black eschar is visible, surrounded by a zone of erythema. The lesion appears well-demarcated, with no visible purulent drainage or ulceration beyond the eschar. Several smaller erythematous macules are visible in the surrounding skin. The findings are consistent with a necrotic lesion, possibly due to an infectious or inflammatory process.
